findings.location: Assumptions and constraints — “The reading, written before any search runs”
findings.problem: The decision rule judges P only against T and K; it omits M even though M is one of the four searches the plan is intended to compare. P can therefore be called “enough” while the direct meaning search performs as well or better, so the rule cannot support a conclusion about the added value of problem search.
findings.suggestion: Include M in the comparator (or explicitly justify why it is excluded) and define the conclusion for ties and intermediate results against all relevant baselines.

findings.location: Assumptions and constraints — “The four searches” and “The measures”
findings.problem: The plan gives incompatible ranking rules for P. It says a book’s place over several sub-problems is its smallest place, but also says P uses its books in the order returned. The existing problem-search merged list is ordered by best score, not by smallest per-sub-problem rank, so these can yield different ranks and hit-at-5 outcomes.
findings.suggestion: Specify one P ranking calculation unambiguously, including tie-breaking, and require the command/report to use it consistently.

findings.problem: The plan leaves the owner’s pair-judging decision unrestricted, while the referenced roadmap makes pair-judging dependent on the trial showing that search alone is not enough. The plan’s “enough” outcome can still lead to pair judging, which drifts from the candidate’s dependency.
findings.suggestion: State that pair judging is proposed only when the recorded trial result shows search alone is not enough, or amend the roadmap through the required direction-change process before allowing another condition.

summary: The plan needs a complete comparison rule, an unambiguous P rank definition, and alignment with the roadmap’s pair-judging dependency.
